channel.title: Field Notes | Chris Garin
channel.description: Brand histories and field notes from Chris Garin.

item.title: The Genius of 'Good Enough': How MR.DIY Took Over the Philippines
item.description: MR.DIY is Malaysian, founded in 2005 by a physics graduate, and it does not franchise. Why it is so cheap, and why there is now one in every Iloilo town.

item.title: The Brand Origins of DALI (2026) | Chris Garin
item.description: DALI went from one store in Santa Rosa, Laguna in 2020 to more than a thousand branches across Luzon, without a single TV ad. Who owns it, and how.

item.title: Partizan: Connecting the Dots, Ten Years Later | Chris Garin
item.description: I scrolled ten years back through my first company’s Facebook page and found a younger version of me already chasing everything I’m chasing now.

item.title: Heatseeker: the tool I built to never face a blank page again | Chris Garin
item.description: For years my ideas died in my notes because I could not build them. So I learned to build. Heatseeker is what came out of it.

item.title: How a Realtor's Postcards Beat His Email Funnel | Chris Garin
item.description: Two realtors, opposite playbooks, same result. The thing that actually works is paying attention to one person at a time.

item.title: I Wasn't Lazy. I Was Scared. | Chris Garin
item.description: I procrastinated for a year before making content again. I thought I was lazy. It was fear wearing a better outfit.

item.title: Pax Silica Explained: What It Is and Why China Is Mad
item.description: What the US-led Pax Silica coalition and the proposed New Clark City hub actually mean for the Philippines, explained simply.

item.title: IMAX in the Philippines: History, Screens, and Locations
item.description: Everything about IMAX in the Philippines: how it arrived in 2006, who owns and runs it, whether it is real IMAX or LieMAX, and where to watch it.

item.title: Who Owns TCL? Country, Owner, and What TCL Stands For
item.description: TCL is a Chinese company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Huizhou. It is not owned by Samsung. The full story of the world's number two TV brand.

item.title: The History of Lazada in the Philippines | Chris Garin
item.description: How Lazada solved cash-on-delivery, fixed Philippine logistics, got bought by Alibaba, and turned a country that distrusted online shopping into one that lives on it.

item.title: Who Owns Oppo, Vivo, Realme and OnePlus? The BBK Story | Chris Garin
item.description: Oppo, Vivo, Realme and OnePlus look like rivals but share one owner: BBK Electronics. How four sibling brands took over Philippine phone shelves.

item.title: Ayala History: From the 1834 Roxas Founding to Ayala Land
item.description: How Ayala went from an 1834 distillery founded by the Roxas family to Ayala Land and the Philippines oldest conglomerate, and who runs it now.

item.title: The Brand Origins of Iloilo Supermart (2026) | Chris Garin
item.description: Iloilo Supermart traces back to Hoskyn's, the first department store in the Philippines. The real 150-year lineage and the Que family behind it.

item.title: The History of Nescafé in the Philippines | Chris Garin
item.description: From an 1881 instant-coffee patent to the 3-in-1 sachet in every sari-sari store. How Nescafé became the default coffee of the Philippines.

item.title: SkyFlakes History: Who Owns It and Is It Really Filipino?
item.description: The full story of SkyFlakes crackers: the M.Y. San origin, who owns it today, why it is a Filipino icon, and even how many holes each cracker has.

item.title: Estate Tax in the Philippines: Why Families Fight Over Inheritance | Chris Garin
item.description: Philippine estate tax quietly tears families apart because nobody plans for it. What it is, why unpaid estate tax freezes property for generations, and what to do about it.

item.title: The Rise (and Fall?) of Pickup Coffee (2026) | Chris Garin
item.description: Pickup Coffee went from one cloud store to 500+ in four years. Now Zus and Jollibee's Compose Coffee are coming for the category it created.

item.title: The History of Rustan's: How the Tantoco Family Built It | Chris Garin
item.description: Rustan's is a portmanteau of Rustia and Tantoco, the couple who founded it in 1952. The story of how a family shop became a Philippine retail institution.

item.title: The History of Megaworld and Andrew Tan | Chris Garin
item.description: How Andrew Tan went from selling cheap liquor to building Megaworld, one of the biggest property developers in the Philippines, and what else he owns.

item.title: The History of National Bookstore and Nanay Coring | Chris Garin
item.description: How Socorro Ramos, known as Nanay Coring, built National Bookstore from a wartime stall into the biggest bookstore chain in the Philippines.

item.title: Who Owns Chooks-to-Go? The Owner and Full History
item.description: Who owns Chooks-to-Go, the company behind it, its tagline, and how the roast chicken brand grew across the Philippines. The complete backstory.

item.title: Dunkin' Donuts vs Mister Donut: The Rivalry Explained | Chris Garin
item.description: Dunkin' Donuts and Mister Donut were founded by two brothers-in-law who fell out. The story behind the rivalry, and how it played out in the Philippines.

item.title: The Brand Origins of Palawan Pawnshop (2026) | Chris Garin
item.description: Bobby Castro did not found Palawan Pawnshop. He bought it for P40,000 in 1985. The full story, from Martial Law activist to 3,800 branches and PalawanPay.

item.title: Who Owns Puregold? The Lucio and Susan Co Story
item.description: Who owns Puregold: the Lucio and Susan Co story, how they founded it, their S&R connection, and how it became a Philippine retail giant.

item.title: GCash History: When It Launched and Who Created It
item.description: GCash history in full: when it launched, who created it, its link to Globe, and how it became the Philippines biggest e-wallet.
